  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms affect mouse navigation performance across five key metrics",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation shows poorest performance across all metrics with lowest success rate (27.3%), highest time-to-target (4.68s), lowest path efficiency (0.31), lowest average speed (10.74), and lowest angular dispersion (0.24)",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms show best overall performance with success rates around 78%, time-to-target around 2.6s, path efficiency around 0.50, and average speed around 12.7",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance with success rates around 67-69%, time-to-target around 3.0-3.1s, and path efficiency around 0.43",
    "Angular dispersion (AD) follows a similar pattern with highest values in Combined (0.40) and Bright Visual Only (0.39), intermediate in ICMS Only (0.35) and Dim Visual Only (0.34), and lowest in Sham (0.24)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sham vs all active stimulation paradigms shows largest performance gap across all metrics",
    "Bright Visual Only vs Dim Visual Only shows substantial difference in success rate (78.5% vs 67.3%) and path efficiency (0.50 vs 0.43)",
    "Combined stimulation shows similar performance to Bright Visual Only across most metrics",
    "ICMS Only performs slightly better than Dim Visual Only but worse than Bright Visual Only"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Active stimulation paradigms significantly improve navigation performance compared to sham, with visual stimulation (particularly bright visual) showing the strongest benefits.     "No information about within-paradigm variability or individual mouse differences",
    "No control for potential confounding factors or experimental conditions"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct statistical hypothesis testing (ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis) with post-hoc comparisons to determine which performance differences between stimulation paradigms are statistically significant"
}
